speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a painful, ulcerative lesion on your leg. To help me understand what is happening, have you had any recent insect bites, or do you have a history of diabetes or vascular disease?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and immunosuppression from corticosteroid use, are you currently experiencing any fever, chills, or systemic illness alongside this painful leg ulcer? DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum (steroid-induced neutropenia with underlying Crohn's disease)

The combination of a rapidly progressive painful ulcer with undermined borders, your history of Crohn's disease, and prior steroid use for uveitis strongly points to Pyoderma Gangrenosum. I am requesting a wound culture to rule out superimposed infection and an MRI of the leg to assess the depth of tissue involvement before we initiate immediate immunosuppressive therapy.
